quiz.title: Apache Airflow
quiz.description: Workflow orchestration with Apache Airflow: DAGs, tasks, operators, scheduling, and dependency management.

questions.question_text: What is Apache Airflow primarily used for?
questions.option_a: Programmatically authoring, scheduling, and monitoring workflows
questions.correct_answer: Programmatically authoring, scheduling, and monitoring workflows

questions.question_text: What does DAG stand for in Airflow?
Why must an Airflow workflow be 'acyclic'?
questions.option_a: So that tasks have a clear order and dependencies never form an infinite loop
questions.option_b: So that tasks can run in a random order
questions.option_c: So that only one task can ever exist
questions.option_d: So that tasks always run forever
questions.correct_answer: So that tasks have a clear order and dependencies never form an infinite loop

questions.question_text: What is a 'task' in an Airflow DAG?
questions.option_a: A single unit of work, such as running a script or querying a database
questions.correct_answer: A single unit of work, such as running a script or querying a database

questions.option_a: A template that defines a single type of task, such as running Python code or a Bash command
questions.option_b: A person who manages the Airflow server
questions.correct_answer: A template that defines a single type of task, such as running Python code or a Bash command

questions.question_text: How are dependencies between tasks typically defined in an Airflow DAG (using the bitshift syntax)?
questions.option_a: Using operators like task_a >> task_b to indicate task_a runs before task_b
questions.option_c: By running all tasks at the exact same time always
questions.option_d: Dependencies cannot be defined in Airflow
questions.correct_answer: Using operators like task_a >> task_b to indicate task_a runs before task_b

questions.option_a: Continuously monitors DAGs and triggers task instances according to their schedule and dependencies
questions.option_d: Replaces the need for a database
questions.correct_answer: Continuously monitors DAGs and triggers task instances according to their schedule and dependencies

questions.question_text: What is a common reason to use Airflow to orchestrate an ETL pipeline?
questions.option_a: It manages scheduling, retries, and dependencies between extract, transform, and load steps
questions.option_b: It removes the need to write any extraction code
questions.option_c: It only works with a single cloud provider
questions.option_d: It cannot be monitored or logged
questions.correct_answer: It manages scheduling, retries, and dependencies between extract, transform, and load steps

questions.question_text: What does the Airflow web UI primarily allow you to do?
questions.option_a: Visualize DAGs, monitor task status, and view logs
questions.correct_answer: Visualize DAGs, monitor task status, and view logs

questions.question_text: What happens if a task in an Airflow DAG fails and retries are configured?
questions.option_a: Airflow can automatically retry the task according to the configured retry policy
questions.option_b: The entire Airflow installation shuts down permanently
questions.option_d: All future runs of any DAG are cancelled
questions.correct_answer: Airflow can automatically retry the task according to the configured retry policy
